text: The authors describe CCS (Burns et al., 2022) as one of the most representative works for unsupervised elicitation, which works by solely using simple logical consistency to find latent knowledge, and say that while it moderately outperforms the zero-shot prompting baseline it still significantly underperforms supervised approaches. Citing Farquhar et al. (2023), they add that CCS and other unsupervised approaches often cannot find knowledge.
title: Wen et al. argue Burns et al.'s CCS, using logical consistency alone, lags supervised methods
